Read an mrgsolve model specification

Source: R/read-mrgsolve.R
pmx_read_mrgsolve.Rd

Reads an mrgsolve model file (.cpp) into the package's representation.

Usage

pmx_read_mrgsolve(file)

Arguments

file

Path to the model file.

Value

A zufapmx_model; see pmx_inspect and pmx_write_mrgsolve().

Details

The reader covers $PROB, $PARAM (plain or @annotated), $THETA, $CMT, $INIT, $MAIN/$PK, $ODE/$DES, $TABLE/$ERROR, $CAPTURE, $PKMODEL, $OMEGA and $SIGMA (with @block), and $NMXML/$NMEXT as sources of NONMEM estimates. Blocks may also be written [ NAME ]. Code is the C++ subset mrgsolve documents for models: declarations and assignments, if/else, arithmetic, comparisons, exp(), log(), log10(), sqrt(), fabs(), pow(), fmin(), fmax(), ETA(n), EPS(n), THETA(n), and the macros dxdt_CMT, F_CMT, ALAG_CMT, R_CMT, D_CMT and CMT_0. Anything else, including $GLOBAL, $PREAMBLE, the nm-vars plugin, int declarations and integer division (3/4), is refused with an error of class zufapmx_parse_error. $PKMODEL may take its parameters from $PARAM directly or from $MAIN.

Recorded as losses of the read: the title, $PLUGIN, $SET, $PARAM descriptions, and $TABLE outputs Y does not use. TIME and SOLVERTIME read as the representation's time, t. $NMXML and $NMEXT resolve a relative path against the working directory, or the model file's with root = "cppfile", as mrgsolve does.

The observation is Y in $TABLE, written over a prediction such as IPRED; its residual model is recognised as for NONMEM. An @annotated $PARAM description of the form [lower, upper], optionally followed by fixed, gives a parameter's bounds, as pmx_write_mrgsolve() writes them.

See also

Other readers: pmx_read_nonmem(), pmx_read_rxode2()

Examples

path <- system.file(
  "corpus", "twocmt-bolus", "model.cpp",
  package = "zufapmx"
)
pmx_read_mrgsolve(path)
#> <zufapmx_model> read from mrgsolve
#> Structure: two-compartment closed form, direct input (ADVAN3 TRANS4)
#> Parameters: 4, initial values only
#> Random effects: ETA1 on CL (exp), ETA2 on V1 (exp)
#> Endpoints: Y (proportional)
